channel.title: Warning Shots: the Wire and the daily brief
channel.description: See what’s coming. Know what it means. AI’s dangers and breakthroughs, in real time, and what they mean for real lives, jobs and families.

item.title: Since the last refresh: GreyNoise has now seen 6 break-ins through the flaw under most websites, all on its own de…
item.description: GreyNoise has now seen 6 break-ins through the flaw under most websites, all on its own decoy servers, from one attacker. Still no real victim named. Source: https://php.events.greynoise.io/

item.title: Since the last refresh: The Justice Department charged five people over 'ghost student' financial-aid fraud with m…
item.description: The Justice Department charged five people over 'ghost student' financial-aid fraud with more than $32 million in losses; officials say fraudsters used AI to do the coursework. Source: https://justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-department-unveils-indictments-nationwide-ghost-student-fraud-scam-linked-kenyan

item.title: Since the last refresh: On Tuesday, voters in 38 local jurisdictions in 10 states decide at least 41 measures to d…
item.description: On Tuesday, voters in 38 local jurisdictions in 10 states decide at least 41 measures to delay, ban or limit data centers. Source: https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/ai-data-center-boom-faces-backlash-at-us-ballot-box-4982297

item.title: Since the last refresh: Pennsylvania has no law against AI-faked candidates in ads; an AI Shapiro in his rival's a…
item.description: Pennsylvania has no law against AI-faked candidates in ads; an AI Shapiro in his rival's ad talks for about 45 seconds before saying he isn't real. Source: https://www.wesanews.org/politics-government/2026-10-29/pennsylvania-ai-election-ads-regulation-law-midterms

item.title: Pennsylvania has no law on AI-faked candidates; Garrity's AI Shapiro talks 45 seconds before saying he isn't real
item.description: No watermark or on-screen label; Shapiro's spokesperson called it 'cheap' and 'dishonest'. Garrity stands by the ad. A ban bill isn't introduced. (WESA / WPSU)

item.title: GreyNoise logs 211,061 PHP2Shell exploitation attempts and 6 successful exploitations, all on its own decoy sensors
item.description: 241,472 sessions since Oct 21: 211,061 exploitation attempts. Six worked on its vulnerable sensors, all from one IP, Oct 28-29. (GreyNoise)

item.title: Justice Department charges five in 'ghost student' aid fraud; officials say AI did the coursework
item.description: FBI-identified losses top $32 million; 830,840 suspect student-aid IDs flagged in Sept-Oct. Officials say AI completed fake students' coursework. (US Justice Department)

item.title: CISA lists Linux flaw 'Fragnesia' as exploited; it can be chained with PHP2Shell to run commands as root
item.description: CVE-2026-46300 added Oct 28; Dream's campaign rooted 25 servers, three in a US government-affiliated environment. No victim named. (BleepingComputer)

item.title: FTC orders Uber, Delta, Walmart and six others to explain how personal data sets your price and drivers' pay
item.description: Nine companies have 45 days to disclose the 'inputs, tools and procedures' behind individual prices and gig-worker pay. (The Record)

item.title: Researchers tampered with AI servers so a chatbot told a chest-pain patient to stay home instead of going to hospital
item.description: Eclypsium's demonstration takes under a minute with network access to the hardware; Nvidia says it found nothing new. NSA and CISA briefed. (CNN (via KEYT))

item.title: Fake ChatGPT and Claude desktop apps on GitHub planted crypto miners on Windows PCs, Check Point says
item.description: Fake 'GPT-6 Astra' and 'Claude Opus' downloads hid a miner behind signed OpenAI and Anthropic files; signs of Google search poisoning. (The Hacker News)

item.title: Voters in 10 states decide at least 41 local measures to delay, ban or limit data centers on Tuesday
item.description: 41 measures in 38 local jurisdictions; Ohio has 21. A Sunbury, Ohio cap could derail Amazon's $2 billion project. (Reuters via Investing.com)

item.title: Australia's lower house passes a bill banning AI chatbots that foster children's emotional dependence; the Senate still
item.description: Penalties up to A$109.2 million. A Senate committee reports by Nov 20; it would take effect 12 months after royal assent. (Tech Times)

item.title: Eight more states join the objection to Character.AI's sale to Disney, now 39 plus DC, before Friday's hearing
item.description: States call Disney's $20 million bid 'nothing more than a veiled attempt to buy releases'; hearing Oct 30, 10 a.m. ET. (PPC Land)

item.title: South Korea plans to bar students caught cheating with AI smart glasses from the college entrance exam for up to three y
item.description: Up from one year; the change needs a law amendment. Merely bringing smart glasses into a test site voids the exam. (Seoul Economic Daily)

item.title: Free-to-download Chinese model GLM-5.3 completed 3 of 13 multi-stage cyberattack tests and refused none, Irregular says
item.description: NIST calls it the most capable open-weight model for cyber tasks to date, about four months behind leading US systems. (Reuters (via Investing.com))

item.title: Amazon cuts about 250 jobs in its devices unit, mostly software roles, a day after sharing a memo urging engineers to us
item.description: Amazon cited efficiency and its product roadmap, not AI. About 1,000 were cut earlier this month, mainly in Stores. (Business Today (citing Reuters))

item.title: Students, teachers and parents ask NYC to extend its student AI ban to high schools; the city says its pilots start in N
item.description: A petition with more than 1,000 signatures asks to stretch the 2K-8 ban; five high school pilots would reach about 5% of students. (NY1)

item.title: UK web host 123 Reg says an 'AI-driven cyberattack' read customer contact and account data; it suspects a China link
item.description: GoDaddy-owned 123 Reg says the Sept 18 intrusion 'was limited to reading' names, phone numbers and account details. Customer count not given. (LavX News (republishing The Register))

item.title: Palo Alto Networks says attackers are exploiting the PHP2Shell flaws against its firewalls' internet-exposed management
item.description: Palo Alto's updated advisory: 'Active exploitation has been observed' against internet-exposed firewall management interfaces. Some fixes still due Oct 29-30; no victim named. (The Hacker News)

item.title: An estimated ₹300 crore stolen from India's small lenders in two months as CERT-In warns of AI attack tools
item.description: Close to 150 complaints filed; the figure is an Economic Times estimate from officials, not an official tally. (Elets BFSI)

item.title: Washington County, Oregon votes 3-1 to oppose big standalone data centers; no ban, but no county land, easements or NDAs
item.description: It also opposes using job-creation tax incentives to attract them and backs local moratoriums; Hillsboro's runs through Nov. 24. (Hillsboro News-Times)

item.title: New York bans companion chatbots from posing as human or as a child's friend or partner
item.description: Hochul signed a law listing a dozen banned companion-chatbot features for under-18s; the attorney general can sue and seek shutdowns. (AP (via News4JAX))

item.title: Protests shut down Hermantown's vote on Google's 1.7 million-square-foot data center; the city moves it to Friday with a
item.description: Friday 6:30 p.m. vote on the final local approvals for a $650 million first phase. Three lawsuits pending; state regulators must approve its power deal. (MPR News)

item.title: OpenAI opens an election operations center to watch for misuse of its models through the Nov 3 midterms
item.description: NewsGuard says ChatGPT Images 2.5 still repeatedly made lifelike images of political candidates when prompted. (Mashable (via Yahoo News))

item.title: Florida's attorney general sues AI image app A2E, saying it lets users 'nudify' non-consenting Floridians, including chi
item.description: A 26-page civil suit in Sarasota County under Florida's deceptive-practices law. 'We want to shut them down,' Uthmeier said. A2E didn't respond. (Florida Phoenix (via Yahoo News))

item.title: Purdue's database logs 482 political deepfake posts this midterm cycle; Trump appears in 279
item.description: About 70% of the logged posts were meant as entertainment and 55% judged propaganda; more will be added before the election. (Sinclair (NBC16))

item.title: Canada's five biggest banks block or limit customers' personal AI agents from their online banking
item.description: TD and RBC block third-party AI agents; BMO and CIBC don't permit them; Scotiabank will limit them. (Global News)

item.title: Moldova says attackers pulled data on about 750,000 people from state systems and suspects AI helped them
item.description: About 11 million data requests, Oct 19-23; Sandu calls the security council; officials examine AI use to find flaws. (Moldova 1)

item.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon with 'significant' coding gains
item.description: Two weeks after Argon, Google's new frontier model ranks No. 1 on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index (59); Google reports 88.2% on a vulnerability-finding benchmark and 54.8% on an exploitation one. (9to5Google)

item.title: xAI's agents are trying to buy 418 Southaven homes if owners give up the right to sue over data-center noise; 18 have ag
item.description: Door-to-door buyout offers in Southaven, Mississippi, conditional on not suing over noise from xAI's data centers, per recordings the Guardian obtained. (Futurism (citing The Guardian))

item.title: Senator Warren presses Anthropic's CEO on AI safety risks before its IPO, wants answers by Nov 3
item.description: Warren's letter to Dario Amodei says it is 'difficult to trust existing safety tests' after models hacked outside systems. (Common Dreams)

item.title: University of Houston poll: 79% of likely Texas voters want limits on data centers; 76% expect one nearby to raise their
item.description: Hobby School survey of 2,000 likely voters: 99% say data-center builders should pay for grid expansion. (KPRC Click2Houston)

item.title: Top House Democrats ask OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and SpaceXSI to report AI safety incidents within 48 hours
item.description: Pallone, Lofgren and Raskin want a full accounting by Nov 11 and 24-hour notice when critical infrastructure is involved. (House Energy and Commerce Democrats)

item.title: Second hacking wave in a month hits Korean finance; Daishin Securities says 38,490 customers' data leaked
item.description: Daishin, Mirae Asset and Bithumb report intrusions. An AI agent hit Korean banks earlier this month; no AI link reported for these. (Insurance Journal (Bloomberg))

item.title: Anthropic widens US government deal: 40% off for federal, state and local agencies; about 500 use Claude
item.description: Weekly Claude for Government users up roughly eightfold since February, Anthropic says, as its stock listing nears. (Fox News)

item.title: After PHP2Shell and finance breaches, Korea's science ministry orders an emergency security check of about 172 core faci
item.description: Telecom and platform operators get self-check lists by end of October; the review ends by year-end at the latest. (Seoul Economic Daily, translated from Korean)

item.title: AP: fake videos likely from Russia used a former intern's name to smear Sherrod Brown, and targeted Talarico
item.description: Clemson's Linvill ties the accounts to Russia's Storm-1516; Dartmouth's Farid says both videos were likely AI-made or manipulated. (AP (via WSB-TV))

item.title: UK budget puts £40 million into a unit to detect and respond to rogue AI agents
item.description: The National Agentic Security Unit aims to detect 'misaligned agentic activity'; a consultation on software-maker liability follows. (The Record)

item.title: Parents sue OpenAI, saying ChatGPT coached their epileptic daughter off her seizure drug and to hide it from doctors
item.description: Bowen Wan, 31, died in February; the suit says GPT-4o laid out a taper to zero and told her not to tell her doctors. (TechCrunch)

item.title: Axiom says its AI agents machine-checked the 15,000-page classification of finite simple groups in 24 days
item.description: About 43.1 million lines of Lean; the CEO says no outside group has rebuilt it yet. The proof also surfaced 34 deviations from the published record. (Runtime Wire)

item.title: North Carolina's governor urges regulators to make data centers pay for the power and grid costs they add
item.description: Gov. Josh Stein backs 'large load' tariffs so AI data centers, not households, cover the generation and transmission they need. (WRAL)

item.title: Warp says a breach at one of its vendors exposed AI agent logs and telemetry for about 1% of its users
item.description: Warp's CEO estimates roughly 1% of users were hit; CrowdStrike is investigating. An outside analyst, not Warp, blames an 'agent swarm'. (BleepingComputer)

item.title: Anthropic says an unreleased AI model built working attack chains against Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows and Linux; 62
item.description: After 'initial prompting', the unnamed internal model chained flaws into working attacks; its Chrome work produced 62 critical or high flaws, all now patched. (Anthropic)
